text.brief: Belgian police arrested the intelligence officer Xu Yanjun on April 1, 2018, when he arrived for a meeting he had set up himself.
text.record: Xu, a deputy division director in the Ministry of State Security, had come to collect design data on GE Aviation's composite fan module for jet engines. The GE engineer he had cultivated was working with the company and the FBI. Belgium extradited Xu, and a jury convicted him of economic espionage and trade secret conspiracies in November 2021 ([United States v. Xu, No. 22-4020 (6th Cir.; govinfo)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-ca6-22-04020/pdf/USCOURTS-ca6-22-04020-1.pdf)). He received 20 years in November 2022 ([United States v. Xu, No. 22-4020 (6th Cir.; govinfo)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-ca6-22-04020/pdf/USCOURTS-ca6-22-04020-1.pdf)). Xu had also directed Ji Chaoqun, a student in Chicago who enlisted in the Army Reserve in 2016, and a jury convicted Ji in September 2022.
text.reading: An engineer reported the approach and let the FBI run it, so the handler walked into a meeting he had arranged himself. The officer's own recruitment turned against him, which is Stratagem 33.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. The design held because the company's security team and the FBI treated the first contact as a shared problem.
text.fix: Give every engineer a fast path to report an approach, and let counterintelligence decide how to use it.
